contract_plain_english: A sufficiently smooth pressure-velocity solution of the first-order acoustics system necessarily has pressure satisfying the derived second-order wave equation p_tt = c^2 p_xx, where c = sqrt(K/rho); the derivation differentiates the two component equations and eliminates the mixed derivative of u.

binders: Sufficiently differentiable real-valued pressure p(x,t) and particle velocity u(x,t).
Constant material parameters K and rho and the sound speed c.
conclusions: The pressure satisfies p_tt = c^2 p_xx.
This pressure equation is the derived second-order wave equation (1.7).
definitions_and_conventions: p_tt is the second partial derivative of pressure with respect to time and p_xx is the second partial derivative with respect to space.
c is the speed of sound and c^2 = K/rho in this acoustic medium.
The eliminated term is the mixed derivative of particle velocity, written u_xt in the source.
hypotheses: p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0.
c = sqrt(K/rho), hence c^2 = K/rho in the intended positive physical regime.
The mixed derivatives used in the elimination exist and agree.
implicit_context: The acoustics model is one-dimensional, linear, homogeneous, and constant-coefficient.
The derivation presupposes second derivatives and interchange of the relevant mixed partials even though no formal smoothness class is named.
The source treats (1.7) as a consequence of (1.5), not as the primary first-order model used later in the book.

details: The conclusion is second order in both time and space and concerns pressure p.
Differentiating the two first-order equations and eliminating the mixed u derivative yields the pressure wave equation.
The spatial second derivative is multiplied by c^2 = K/rho.

undebatable_constraints: The dependent variable in (1.7) is pressure p.
The equation must be p_tt = c^2 p_xx, with second derivatives and the squared sound speed.
The conclusion is obtained from both equations of system (1.5) by mixed-derivative elimination.
The coefficient c must retain its acoustic definition c = sqrt(K/rho).
The source claim is a consequence for solutions of the first-order acoustics system, not an unconditional identity for arbitrary p.
